text:
alex_support: Hey team — customer (acct 8246) opened a billing dispute: invoice shows ~4.9M billed tokens but our served-token dashboard for their app shows ~3.1M. They say nothing else changed. Curious if continuous-batching + prefix/KV prefetch could explain the gap.

maria_billing: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the invoice id and a few sample request_ids? I can start tracing the ledger.

alex_support: Invoice ID: INV-2025-8246-07. Sample request ids: rQp-3a7, rQp-3a8, rQp-3f2 (from the customer's app logs). Customer says most traffic is chat-like short prompts (avg prompt tokens ~8, completion avg ~45).

dan_runtime: quick hypothesis: if the continuous-batcher prefetches prefixes into KV cache before emitting tokens, our metering pipeline might count prefetch tokens as 'served' for billing, but the live served-token metric (consumer-facing) dedupes hits later when the cache answers subsequent requests, leading to a mismatch. also TTL windows on KV buckets can cause bursts of prefetch that never get consumed.

alex_support: Can you explain how prefetch would get billed? I thought billing only counts tokens that the model actually generates.

dan_runtime: short answer: normally yes, but we have two paths: 1) emission-meter (counts tokens when the runtime emits tokens to the API response stream) 2) prefetch-meter (counts tokens when the batcher warms KV/prefix predictions and requests key material from the model backend to prime cache). Prefetch tokens are currently forwarded to the billing pipeline as 'served' because they pass through the same token-logger pipeline before we mark them as pre-emit. If the subsequent real request hits a warmed cache, the emission path doesn't emit those tokens again -> dashboard shows lower served-token count.

maria_billing: ugh. Any way to prove this for the customer? They want a concrete explanation or refund.

dan_runtime: steps i used to repro locally:
```
# reproduce script (bash)
for i in {1..200}; do
echo "{\"prompt\": \"hello $i\"}" | curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Request-Id: repro-$i" -H "X-Enable-Prefetch: 1" -d @- >/dev/null &
done
# then watch metering stream
kubectl logs -l app=metering -c metering | grep "prefetch" | grep repro
```
This shows prefetch events with tokens billed but later emission logs show cache-hit and no emission for many of those requests. Also check `kv-cache.ttl` config — if TTL is short we get a lot of rewarm activity.

alex_support: Did you find which internal flag is responsible? The customer insists they never toggled any feature.

dan_runtime: Could be the batcher rollout we did last week — we enabled `continuous_batcher_prefetch=true` in region eu-west-1 for better latency on small prompts. That change is in release notes but easy to miss. When the batcher sees similar prefixes it fires prefetch. If the billing pipeline doesn't de-duplicate prefetch vs emission, it inflates billed tokens.

maria_billing: Ok, file added: TICKET-7529, tags: billing, metering, eu-west-1, continuous-batcher. I'll put a temporary hold on invoicing and draft a note to the customer while we investigate.

ashley_sre: @dan_runtime can you confirm the exact export name in stackdriver/kinesis we should grep for? I'll create an infra alert if we see >10% discrepancy in any customer over 1h.

dan_runtime: logs: look for `metering.event.type=token_prefetch` and `metering.event.type=token_emission`. Also correlate by `x-request-id`. Quick query: `select sum(tokens) from metering where event_type='token_prefetch' and account=8246 and ts > '2025-07-01'` vs emission.

ops_bot: Incident created: INC-9244 (metering-prefetch-inflation) — assigned to dan_runtime + maria_billing.

maria_billing: Next steps i recommend: 1) correlate prefetch vs emission by X-Request-Id for a 24h window 2) check kv-cache.ttl for the customer's deployment (short TTL -> more rewarms) 3) run repro with `X-Enable-Prefetch: 0` in a staging copy to confirm drop in billed tokens 4) if confirmed, propose invoice adjustment for prefetch window while we patch.

alex_support: I'll send the customer an interim message: "We're investigating a prefetch vs emission accounting gap. We'll provide a full reconciliation within 48h and have a ticket open: TICKET-7529 / INC-9244." :thumbsup:

ashley_sre: FYI infra mitigation: we'll add a dedupe step in metering that marks `token_prefetch` events as provisional and only commit billing if no subsequent cache-hit prevents emission within TTL window. I'll start a PR.

dan_runtime: I'll attach repro logs & a short patch suggestion: switch metering ingestion to tag prefetch events with `prefetch=true` and emit a compensating negative metric if a subsequent `token_emission` is suppressed by a cache hit.

maria_billing: Good. Once we have numbers, i'll propose a credit. For now customer is satisfied with the transparency.
